name: Virtual Location Scouting
title: Virtual Location Scouting
answer: Virtual location scouting is the practice of using generative image and video models, along with 3D tools, to preview or invent places for a photo or film shoot. It covers matching light, weather, architecture, and terrain to a creative brief, so a photographer or director can plan shots without travelling. The work overlaps with concept art, previsualization, and set design, and it often blends real reference photos with synthetic ones. It is part of the broader field of photography and hyper-realism, where the goal is a believable image rather than a documentary record.

sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on a mix of cloud GPUs and local workstations, because image and video generation is compute heavy. Practitioners use text to image models, video models, and 3D engines such as Blender or Unreal Engine, sometimes alongside map data from services like Google Earth. The site currently tracks 1000 live image generation models, which gives a sense of how many options exist for generating a location. Storage and bandwidth matter too, since high resolution stills and short flythroughs add up quickly.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: A typical session starts with a brief that names the location type, time of day, and mood, then the artist writes prompts or supplies reference images. They generate many candidates, then refine the best ones with inpainting, control nets, or 3D blocking to fix perspective and lighting. Real photos or map data can be mixed in to keep scale and geography plausible. The output is usually a set of stills or a short animatic that the director or client can review. Iteration is fast, so the location can be adjusted many times before any travel or set build.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk around virtual location scouting are unsettled, because generated images may resemble real, private, or trademarked places. Provenance matters: keeping a record of prompts, seeds, and model versions helps show how an image was made. If a real location is used as a reference, a release or permit may still be required for the actual shoot. The site tracks 92 active intellectual property lawsuits across AI, which is a reminder that ownership and infringement questions are still being tested. Practitioners often treat generated locations as previsualization, not as a substitute for legal clearance.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction is toward tighter integration with real time engines and virtual production, where a generated location can be explored on an LED wall. Newer methods like Gaussian splatting and neural radiance fields are making it easier to turn a few photos into a navigable 3D scene. Generative video will let scouts produce moving camera tests, not just stills. As the tools mature, the line between scouting and final capture will blur, and rights and provenance practices will need to keep pace.
